D.t: Cindy Holscher leads by 1.7 in the forecast and wins 60% of simulations. The cushion is about 19,321 votes; a one point swing is about 5,750 voters changing sides.
In 8 of 10 simulations the result lands between R +6.7 and D +9.9. A normal polling error decides it.
The polls page average is R +3.5. Your best recent poll is Global Strategy Group (D) at D +0.5; your worst is On Point Polling at R +6.5. 7 polls in the last 30 days.

The biggest vote banks for Democrats: Johnson, a projected net 86,368 votes; Douglas, a projected net 31,705 votes; Wyandotte, a projected net 24,136 votes. Every point of extra turnout here is worth more than persuasion anywhere else.

D.h: Where you run behind the 2024 map
D.t: Against the 2024 presidential vote, Cindy Holscher runs furthest behind in McPherson, Butler, Miami. That is where the forecast sees voters who backed your side two years ago and have not come back yet.

Groups big enough to move the race: White voters, 88% of voters, 47 to 51, where a 5 point gain is worth 4.38 points; Voters who cast ballots in 2022 and 2024, 70% of voters, 49 to 50, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.49 points; Voters who find daily costs hard to afford, 59% of voters, 56 to 42, where a 5 point gain is worth 2.94 points.

The forecast's worst groups for Cindy Holscher: Immigration voters 20 to 78, Small counties 31 to 66, Voters who can afford daily costs 40 to 58. Cutting the loss here is often cheaper than winning new groups.
